Subject: Proposal: lightweight client priority hint + runtime debug hooks (OliveTech POC)

Hi team —

Quick context: OliveTech is mid-POC and experiencing intermittent rate spikes that push them to fallback variants; their app wants to mark a subset of requests as higher business priority (payment confirmation flows) so they can guarantee lower tail latency during bursts. They asked if we can accept a small, opt-in client hint that the app sets per request (non-auth-affecting) so the routing layer and runtime can treat it as a tie-breaker for fast-path selection.

What I'm proposing for discussion (minimal surface):
- SDK/API: add optional header X-RW-Priority: <0..100> (missing = default 50). No auth change.
- Gateway: the routing layer may use the hint to prefer lower-latency model variants if capacity available.
- Runtime: emit telemetry on accepted hints and (important) a debug hook that can be toggled per-customer so we can trace how hints influence routing decisions.

Questions for platform/runtime:
1) Is exposing a simple header feasible without breaking batching behavior?
2) Can runtime expose a per-customer canary flag so this only applies for OliveTech during initial trials?
3) Any telemetry/trace impact we should expect (cardinality, ingestion cost)?

Marissa — customer asks for an implementation timeline this month. Logan/Sean — need your read on technical risk and a suggested rollback/canary plan. I'm attaching a short SDK patch prototype and the customer's PO request.

Thanks,
Jordan

Thanks for the write-up. Quick take from routing/runtime:

- Adding an optional header X-RW-Priority is straightforward at the gateway layer; we can surface it in request metadata without auth changes. It should be strictly advisory (we won't allow it to override quota or auth decisions).

- Main technical risk: per-request priority can reduce batching efficiency if it causes requests to be split across lanes. However, since OliveTech will only mark ~5% high priority, the net batching loss is likely small. We should instrument batching delta in the canary.

- Telemetry: recommend emitting a boolean field in traces (rw.priority_present) and the value (rw.priority_value) with a low-cardinality cap (only record values 1-5 buckets to control cardinality). We can also emit a routed_variant tag. This will allow post-mortem without high ingestion cost.

- Canary plan (high level):
  1) Gateway accepts header but it's noop unless customer flag enabled.
  2) Enable flag for OliveTech in staging -> run for 48 hours, measure latency tail and batching impact.
  3) If telemetry OK, enable in production with canary on 1% of traffic, increase to 10% after 24h.

I've opened a short doc with specifics: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cOliveTech-POC-priority-hint (see runtime-canary-plan.md).

If Sean is okay with the runtime instrumentation and the fallback behavior, we can propose timeline to Marissa. I estimate ~2w of engineering (gateway + flagging + telemetry) if we prioritize it.

—Logan

On Thu, Nov 5, 2026 at 2:28 PM Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Adding an optional header X-RW-Priority is straightforward at the gateway layer...

Agree with Logan's assessment. A few runtime notes / concerns from the serving-runtime side:

1) Batching: Our batcher groups by model variant, sequence length, and payload shape. Introducing priority hints as a grouping dimension will fragment batches. To avoid that, the runtime should treat the hint as advisory for routing only and not as a hard grouping key in the batcher. We'll need logic that, during load, will still allow high-priority requests to join existing batches if latency estimates remain acceptable. That logic adds complexity but is doable.

2) Resource fairness: we need a guardrail so high-priority requests don't starve regular traffic. I propose a soft quota (e.g., max 10% of GPU slots reserved for priority across a shard) that is configurable per-customer.

3) Debug hooks: exposing a per-customer 'priority_debug' flag that turns on detailed tracing + per-request routing decision logs is fine, but those logs must be scoped and TTL'd; they should not be immediately forwarded to global telemetry (push to internal debug sink first).

4) Canary: I'm fine with the 48h staging + 1% prod canary. We'll need the ops runbook for rapid rollback. I've attached a canary plan draft (runtime-canary-plan.md).

If we can keep the header handling out of the tight batch path (gateway annotates metadata; runtime consults but doesn't re-bucket indiscriminately), the perf hit should be small. Otherwise, it's a non-starter.

—Sean
